children: FPFX Tech has added Tickblaze to its prop trading infrastructure, linking the platform’s trading interface and execution layer with the evaluation rules, breach monitoring and funded-account workflows managed through PropAccount.
London's trading industry is coming home!
The partnership separates the trading front end from the back-office rules. Tickblaze provides desktop, web, and mobile trading interfaces, along with order handling and execution.
FPFX continues to manage account rules, evaluations, funded-account transitions, reporting and other operational processes through PropAccount.
The connection addresses a practical issue for prop firms operating large numbers of evaluation accounts.

Trading activity must stay aligned with the back office that enforces daily loss limits, maximum drawdowns and other challenge conditions. Otherwise, a trader could keep using an account that should have been restricted.

The companies said the integration is designed to maintain consistent account states and rule enforcement, although they did not disclose the latency between a trading event and the corresponding restriction.
Tickblaze Gains Access to FPFX Clients

The arrangement brings Tickblaze into the FPFX client base across futures, foreign exchange and contracts for difference. It gives prop firms using FPFX another platform option without requiring them to replace their existing account-management workflows.
For Tickblaze, the partnership provides access to firms using FPFX infrastructure, including firms operating in the FX and CFD segment.
The platform has previously focused heavily on futures and earlier this year added direct access to CME Group market data, including Level 1 and Level 2 data delivered inside its own environment.

FPFX, meanwhile, expands a platform range that already includes MT5, cTrader, DXtrade, Match-Trader, Rithmic and Tradovate. These platforms connect to PropAccount’s risk engine, administrative dashboard and account-management systems, according to the company’s current integration information.

The partnership announcement does not identify a first prop firm already operating the combined setup. The companies also did not provide a launch date, technical connection protocol or service-level figures for synchronising breaches and account-status changes.
Tickblaze already lists FPFX Tech among its back-office and CRM partners. That shows the partnership has been listed publicly, but neither company has named a live client using the combined setup.

title: FPFX Adds Tickblaze as New Platform Option for Prop Firms
